title: Third complete diplomatic article-text transcription batch
transcription_scope: complete article text for visually bounded entries; source spelling and punctuation retained; typographic line wrapping not encoded
provenance_note: AI-assisted visual transcription from the supplied Steffel facsimile. The facsimile is authoritative; supplied OCR was used only as a reading aid. Ambiguous historical glyphs or Rarámuri spellings are explicitly flagged and remain pending independent human/philological and linguistic verification.

records.article_diplomatic: Ergreifen. Tſchepi. Es iſt ergriffen. Tſchapirúc. Ergriffen, tſchapirúgameke.
records.uncertainty_note: The Rarámuri consonant sequence and acute accent in the perfect forms are visually clear enough for a working diplomatic reading but remain pending human verification.

records.article_diplomatic: Etwas. Rachpébi, rachpébi, piléke, pilé nanamuti.
records.uncertainty_note: The initial letter of the second rachpébi-like form is difficult in the scan; the reading is provisional.
The short Rarámuri equivalent is visually ambiguous in the final two characters; Ulalä is retained as the current facsimile-based reading.

records.article_diplomatic: Faſttag. Jumaguáliki. Die Tarahumaren gebrauchen ſich auch dieſes Wortes um einen großen Faſttag anzudeuten, obgleich ein Faſttag eigentlich Jomeiki heißt.
records.uncertainty_note: The headword is the fasting-day article (Faſttag), distinct from the later Feſttag article on the same page.
The medial s/long-s sequence in the Rarámuri form is difficult in the scan and remains provisional.

records.article_diplomatic: Faulenzen. Naſſinäe. Faulenzend im Faulenzen begriffen, naſſinaja. Faulen. Mujá. Es faulet ſchon. Mujába. Faul, gefault. Mujáianeke.
records.uncertainty_note: Several medial s/long-s shapes and the final Mujáianeke form are retained as provisional facsimile readings pending human verification.
The medial consonant/vowel sequence in Bouguapiki is small in the facsimile and remains provisional.
The Rarámuri equivalent is retained as Teculéke from the facsimile; human verification is still required.
The printed line-break hyphen in Cajé-uopa is treated as typographic and not encoded in the continuous diplomatic text.
This feast-day article is distinct from the earlier Faſttag fasting-day article on the same page.

records.article_diplomatic: Feuer. Náiki. Feuer machen, naige. Man muß Feuer ſchlagen. Tſchichpiopa, ſ. Grieß.
records.uncertainty_note: The Rarámuri form in the Feuer-schlagen phrase is visually compact; Tſchichpiopa is retained as a provisional diplomatic reading.
